The present application has been filed by the appellant seeking suspension of sentence during the pendency of the appeal.

2. By way of present appeal, the appellant seeks to assail the judgement of conviction dated 20.07.2023 and the order on sentence dated 04.09.2023 whereby the appellant was convicted under section 376 (2)(i) IPC and Section 6 POCSO Act.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that testimony of the child victim (PW-1) is not reliable as she has not specified as to what wrong act has been committed against her, except that the appellant being the son of the landlord has taken her inside the room.
He submits that even it is the victim's mother (PW-2) who has stated that the children often used to go to the appellant's room to watch TV.
He further submits that the Trial Court has erred in relying upon the deposition of the brother of the child victim who has materially improved upon his statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

Further, the MLC (Ex.PW-4/A) of the child victim also does not lend any support to the case of the prosecution as there is no external injury noted in the same and that internal examination was denied by the victim.

He further submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case as there were financial disputes between the families of appellant and victim with respect to non-payment of rent, regarding which suggestions were given.
Lastly, it is submitted that the appellant has undergone around 3 years of incarceration.
4. The application is contested by the learned APP for the State, who is duly assisted by Mr. Kumar Sahilash, learned counsel appointed by DHCLSC to represent the victim.

It is submitted that the victim is a special child who has deposed that the appellant has committed 'galat kaam' with her,
which also finds corroboration in the deposition of the victim's brother.

5. I have heard the learned counsels for the parties and also gone through the statements of the child victim (PW-1), her brother (PW-5) and mother (PW-2) recorded during the investigation as well as under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and deposition before the Court.
As noted above, the MLC does not

There is no FSL Report on record.

Keeping in view the totality of the facts and circumstances, the sentence of the appellant is directed to be suspended during the pendency of appeal on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court/Duty Judicial Magistrate/Link Judicial Magistrate/Jail Superintendent and also subject to the further following conditions:-
(i) In case of change of residential address, the appellant shall promptly inform the same to the concerned Investigating Officer as well as to this Court.
(ii) The appellant shall regularly appear before the Court as and when the appeal is taken up for hearing.
(iii) The appellant will not get in touch directly or indirectly with the victim.
(iv) The appellant shall also provider his contact number to the IO and shall remain available on that number.
7. With the above directions, the application is disposed of.
